title: jurisdictional-sink-orchestrator: idempotent reconciler + terraform module hooks for private installs
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Private installations running in multi-region VPCs need deterministic, auditable wiring of audit-log export sinks per jurisdiction and a reconciler that is safe to re-run during installer upgrades and rollbacks. Current behaviour relied on imperative hooks in the installer which caused drift when upgrades failed mid-flight and made it difficult to guarantee retention policies in cross-region setups. This PR introduces a jurisdiction-aware sink orchestration controller and wiring hooks for the private installer + Terraform modules so audit sinks are created and reconciled idempotently.

Summary of changes: 1) Add a small long-running reconciler (go controller) that watches AuditSink CRs and desired sink mapping from the installer; it performs create/update/delete with strong idempotency guarantees and emits detailed audit events (sink-reconciler.* metrics). 2) Extend terraform modules with new outputs and lifecycle-driven hooks so the private-installer can emit a desired-state manifest into the cluster (terraform/modules/audit_sink/*). 3) Helm chart changes: templates now include jurisdiction labels, retention annotations, and optional lifecycle hooks to defer reconciliation until KMS/secret rotation completes. 4) Installer: on the private-installer side we add a declarative sink-write step that applies the desired-state manifest and waits for the reconciler to report success; this replaces the previous ad-hoc shell provisioning. 5) Tests and e2e: add deterministic e2e that simulates mid-upgrade failures and validates rollback idempotency and retention enforcement.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implemented with retries and backoff, idempotent create/update path - [x] Terraform module hooks and docs added - [x] Helm templates updated for jurisdiction and retention annotations - [x] Installer wiring uses desired-state manifest for reconciliation - [x] Unit + e2e tests added and passing - [x] tfsec and helm linting addressed (one warning suppressed with justification)

Deployment notes: - This is backward compatible: the reconciler will adopt existing sinks by matching labels, so rollout can be done with a simple Canary (deploy reconciler -> enable terraform desired-state output -> flip installer to use manifest). - For air-gapped installs the reconciler image is included in the private registry bundle; ensure registry credentials are present prior to enabling the controller. - KMS-backed sinks: reconciler respects annotated kms_key_ref and will wait for secret readiness before finalizing sink wiring.

Rollback behavior: the reconciler is intentionally conservative: on deletion it removes only sink resources it created or owns (ownerReferences + managed-by label). If an installer rollback is triggered mid-upgrade, re-running the installer applies the same desired-state manifest and the reconciler converges back to the prior state without orphaning temporary resources.

Related work and references: Linear tickets ENG-2147 and ENG-2153 track the reconciler and terraform integrations. See internal design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG-2147/jurisdictional-sink-orchestration and runbook: docs/private/audit-sink-orchestrator.md

Why this is different from previous PRs: previous changes focused on retention lifecycles and sink rotation; this change focuses on making sink wiring declarative and upgrade/rollback safe at the installer and terraform boundaries so compliance operators can guarantee retention and export topology after any control-plane operation.

release_notes:
- Add jurisdiction-aware sink reconciler for private deployments (idempotent, adoption-safe).
- Terraform module outputs to emit desired-state manifests for installer-driven reconciliation.
- Helm chart updates: jurisdiction labels and retention annotations.
- Installer change: declarative sink apply + wait for reconciler.
- E2E tests for upgrade/rollback idempotency.
security_implications: The reconciler enforces retention annotations and respects KMS key readiness. New controller requires role bindings; installer deploys a least-privilege service account. TFSEC flagged a potential IAM scope which is suppressed with justification — see tfsec/suppressions.yaml for details. Audit events emitted by the reconciler include sink create/update/delete with operator identity for forensic tracing.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout recommended: deploy reconciler in a single region, enable desired-state output on terraform for one tenant, validate adoption via tests/e2e/verify-adoption.sh. For rollback, re-run installer with previous manifest — reconciler will converge back. Ensure private registry image is present for air-gapped installs before enabling controller.
